title: A push delivers the orchestrator's whole HEAD, and nothing can withhold a path from a member
foundBy: feature request from another agent, relayed by the user (host); the clone probe below is this session's

evidence.verified: TestWithheldPathsAreRefusedBeforeCreate and TestValidateRefusesADeclarationThatIsNotAPath pass under `go test ./internal/cli/ -count=1`. TestPushNamesTheCommitRefusesWithheldPathsAndLogs passes under `go test ./cmd/cs-campaign-member/ -count=1`. It shows a named commit arriving without its descendant. It shows a push carrying a withheld file, deleted again later, refused with the member's ref and objects unchanged. It shows a merge of the member's own work at the withheld path passing. It finds four log entries, each with member, repository and commit. TestDeliveriesAreLogEvents passes under `go test ./dispatch-viewer/... -count=1`. The full gate, `make check`, passes. `make test-smoke` passes in 452 seconds on the committed cassettes, none of which drives a push.

resolution: A repository or snapshot entry takes a `withhold` list of files, directories or globs. `validate` and `create` refuse a repository whose history carries one on any ref (SPEC R120a). They also refuse a repository whose object store keeps objects no ref reaches, and a snapshot whose tree holds one. `push` takes `--commit`, and delivers that commit and nothing after it (R120b). It refuses when any object it would newly deliver sits at a withheld path, judged against the refs the member already holds (R120c). Every delivery and refusal is a `delivered` or `refused` log entry with the member, repository and commit (R120d), and the viewer draws them on the log row. Withdraw was dropped. A refusal, a named commit and a log make a wrong delivery something to record, and a prune cannot reach a member that merged or read what arrived. The sandbox clone that copies objects no ref reaches is an upstream matter, left unfiled.
details:
`cs-campaign-member push <agent> [repo]` sends the orchestrator's HEAD to the member at `refs/campaign/orchestrator`. The orchestrator cannot name another commit. A push carries the commit's whole history, so every path on that line arrives in the member's clone whether or not the member merges it.

A campaign can be designed so that one member must never see certain files the orchestrator holds, such as a directory of expected results. One push from the wrong checkout delivers them with the history. Nothing refuses it, nothing records it, and a corrective push to an earlier commit is refused as non-fast-forward. Such a campaign can only find a breach afterwards, by scanning clones, and the log gives it nothing to scan.

The push is not the only route. A member's repository is a full bare clone of the host repository, every branch included, and the profile's `ref` picks the checkout rather than the history. A withheld path that exists on any branch of the host repository is therefore in every member's clone at create. The clone is also made from a local path, which copies the object store as it stands. A probe on git 2.53 showed the difference: a blob dropped by `git reset --hard`, reachable only from the reflog, was present in a `git clone --bare <path>` and absent from a `git clone --bare file://<path>`. A ref walk cannot see such an object.

What would help, in order:

- A `withhold` list on a member's repository and snapshot entries. `validate` and `create` hold it against every object reachable from every ref of the host repository, and refuse a host repository that holds objects no ref reaches.
- A push that refuses when any object it would newly deliver sits at a withheld path, judged against the refs the member already holds.
- A log entry for every delivery and every refusal, naming the member, the repository, the commit and the outcome.
- A `--commit` flag, so a push can name what it sends.

The fence covers the git channel only. The text of every `send` is already in the archive, and the tool cannot stop a model from pasting a file into a dispatch.

notes.text: The fence was proved on a live two-seat campaign, both seats on kimi-k3 over Fireworks, with Firecracker members on the slim image. `validate` refused a tainted profile naming the member, the path and the commit. The orchestrator's push of a branch carrying the hold-out was refused and logged, and its push of the clean branch with `--commit` was delivered and logged. Three facts were read from the agent's clone before destroy. The delivered commit was present, the refused commit and the hold-out blob were absent, and no history existed under the withheld path. The agent checked out the delivered ref and reported it, and the orchestrator's reply carried the outcome `campaign-met`. The viewer site built from the archive shows both delivery events. The run cost $0.59 by opencode's accounting.
